correctness.rationale: From the explicit commutator, centralizer equality is exactly rowspace equality; the four disjoint cases d=a=f=0, d=0 and (a,f) nonzero, d nonzero and (a,f)=0, d nonzero and (a,f) nonzero determine every rowspace and fiber. In the rank-three case the parameters alpha,phi,gamma are intrinsically recovered from the unique intersection with (A,D,F) and the normalized remaining row. Summed element fibers equal \(q^6\). Matrix-multiplication-based finite-field enumeration independently confirms the complete table over q=2,3,4,5,7, including characteristic 2 and a proper extension. No finite test is treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Complete rowspace equality and fiber classification was not found in inspected primary sources or mathematical statement-overlap searches. Majeed–Ramkumar 2026 Table 1 already covers centralizer orders, so these are not original. Their clique partition likely implies some codimension-three counts for prime fields, but neither Table 1 nor the inspected §5–6 states the full embedded-centralizer equality spectrum or its unique anomalous codimension-two fiber; extending the proof to all finite field orders also requires a field-linear argument. Dutta–Basnet–Nath treats <=5-centralizer rings. Anil Kumar–Prajapati 2015 already explicitly count \(q^2(q-1)\) equal-centralizer classes within their N2 subset of UT4(q) and classify a separate regular subset, so these subresults are not original. The claim here is only the COMPLETE whole-algebra embedded-centralizer spectrum and its full fiber partition. Kundu–Naik–Singh applies to algebras with exactly two breadth values, unlike this algebra with four. Bhunia counts conjugacy classes rather than equality. A broader unlocated theorem remains a publication-priority risk.
residual_risks: The prior Anil Kumar–Prajapati 2015 same-group partial equivalence classification is substantial; an unstated short summation of the remaining partial cases may narrow novelty further. The present proof explicitly addresses all remaining types and their fibers.

Majeed–Ramkumar 2026 gives a detailed commuting-graph decomposition for UT4(p), and some subcase centralizer counts might follow by adapting it; the current theorem distinguishes embedded equality explicitly and includes all prime powers, but the possibility of an immediate unpublished consequence remains.
An unlocated higher-level centralizer-lattice theorem for unitriangular groups could subsume the result; no globally exhaustive uniqueness claim is made.
Publication coverage is not globally exhaustive. An unlocated result about equality classes of centralizer kernels may affect novelty.

value.rationale: Distinct centralizer count is a natural finite-ring and algebra-group invariant. The complete equality classification and canonical exceptional codimension-two kernel distinguish embedded commutants beyond their sizes or the commuting probability, providing a natural complete classification for a canonical noncommutative nilpotent matrix algebra over every finite field. The full integer polynomial and all fiber multiplicities support exact group/algebra comparisons, rather than just a narrow numerical instance.
